findings.title: The per-account cap gate's use of the per-tick resolved map is asserted by nothing: reverting it to the platform constant leaves all 61 cases green, and lets a sub-default-capped account release past its configured cap
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Two independent survivors on an EXECUTED line (rt-11 M10, rt-12 M15). Not equivalent and not an unexecuted branch: line 1305 runs for every candidate account in almost every case, and only the VALUE differs. Reachable and meaningful in production — an account configured at 5 with 3 attempts today passes the scan arm (3 < 5), so the gate is what bounds it; under the mutant `counters.account` becomes 10 - 3 = 7 instead of 5 - 3 = 2, and with >= 3 rendered rows in the batch the account releases up to 7 and ends the day at 10 attempts against a configured cap of 5 — a silent breach of the enforced cap, and the exact 'arm and gate disagree about one account's number' failure the intake's third invariant names. Every existing fixture is blind to it because each one has at most ONE rendered row available, so the row supply, not the counter, bounds `released`. Fix: one case seeding a configured cap of 2 with 0 attempts and >= 3 rendered rows in a single batch, asserting released === 2 and withheldByReason.account_cap >= 1; that kills both M10 and M15.

findings.title: The new 'lockstep pin' cannot fail on the drift it exists to catch, and its only live assertion is an array ORDER its own docstring disclaims
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Proven in both directions. M12 removed SubscriptionStatus.TRIALING from FULL_ACCESS_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES — verbatim the drift the case's own comment names ('a status admitted by one and refused by the other') — and this case PASSED; the kill came from three pre-existing cases. M12b reordered the array to [TRIALING, ACTIVE], a behaviour-preserving edit, and this case was the SOLE failure of 18, while src/lib/shared/subscription-status.ts:64 states 'Order is `active` then `trialing` and is not meaningful'. Both of its assertions compare the array against a list derived from `subscriptionGrantsFullAccess`, which is itself implemented over that same array (subscription-status.ts:85) — true by construction for any array of canonical statuses in enum order. This is a Duty-2 order assertion with no contract AND a vacuous claim cited in the branch's evidence as the lockstep guarantee. Fix: assert the members against a literal expectation and drop the order coupling (`expect(new Set(FULL_ACCESS_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES)).toEqual(new Set([SubscriptionStatus.ACTIVE, SubscriptionStatus.TRIALING]))`), and delete the predicate-derived comparison rather than keeping a tautology.

findings.title: Both account-level gates in runAccountArm are now unreachable from every test: each can be deleted whole with all 61 cases still green
findings.reason: M8 deleted the subscription gate (1314-1318) and M9b deleted the cap entry gate (1306-1309); both mutants passed 61/61. The scan now refuses exactly the accounts these gates refuse, so the gates never execute under test. Proof that the assertions moved rather than doubled: under M13 (scan-level subscription counter removed) the case titled 'does not release when the subscription does not grant full access' FAILS — i.e. that case is now satisfied by the scan, not by the gate it is named after. Same for the locked gate-order case, whose rounds 3 and 4 are now decided by the scan's FILTER precedence rather than by runAccountArm's statement order, so its title over-claims what it measures. This matters because the gates are the only defence against a status or attempt count changing between the scan (release.ts:1402) and the account arm — `apply-subscription-state.ts` runs on the same worker and the phase awaits many times in between — and invariant #11 names the entitlement gate specifically. Adjudication needed: either keep the gates and add a case that reaches them (e.g. lapse the account between scan and arm via a seam), or accept that they are now unreachable defence-in-depth and say so in the docstring instead of leaving two test titles describing gates they no longer exercise.

findings.title: False claim in a changed docstring: `readResolvedAccountCaps` is said to have 'four predicates' matching loadSolicitationAccountDefault; it has three
findings.reason: The query at release.ts:1733-1736 carries THREE predicates: `persona = 'solicitation'`, `action_class = 'sending'`, `location_id IS NULL`. `loadSolicitationAccountDefault` (src/lib/auto-approval/solicitation-settings.ts:270-273) carries FOUR — the fourth is `account_id`, deliberately absent here because this read is platform-wide. The sentence whose whole job is to warn the next reader about row-identity drift misstates the identity it is comparing, and the difference it glosses over (a per-account read became a cross-account one) is exactly what the tenant-scope allowlist entry exists for.

findings.title: False unconditional claim in two places: 'the lane issues fewer statements per tick, not more' / 'the lane's query count per tick went DOWN'
findings.reason: `readAccountDailySendCap` ran once per CANDIDATE account — zero times on a tick with no candidates. `readResolvedAccountCaps` runs once per tick UNCONDITIONALLY at release.ts:1402, after the three phase-level gates (flag, breaker, ceiling) but before the scan. So on a tick that passes those gates with no candidate accounts the count goes 0 -> 1, i.e. UP; with exactly one candidate account it is unchanged; it only falls from two candidate accounts upward. Both the arch-review-log row and the tenant-scope allowlist justification at scripts/ci/tenant-scope-allowlist.ts:507 state it without that condition, and the allowlist reason is load-bearing paperwork for a cross-account read. Fix: qualify both ('from two candidate accounts per tick upward'), or drop the claim.

findings.title: The new platform-wide read's row-identity predicate is untested and the query has no deterministic tie-break, so a location-scoped policy row could silently become the account's cap for both the arm and the gate
findings.reason: M11 dropped `AND location_id IS NULL` and all 61 cases passed (rt-15). The schema permits a location-scoped solicitation/sending row: migration 091:508's persona CHECK does not constrain `location_id`, and migration 074:78-80 adds `auto_approval_policies_one_location_override` precisely for one row per location. `readResolvedAccountCaps` has no ORDER BY and no LIMIT, so with two rows for one account the `resolved.set` loop at release.ts:1737 keeps whichever Postgres returned last — and that number then drives BOTH the scan's HAVING and every per-account gate for that account. No write path creates such a row today (`upsertSolicitationAccountDefault`, solicitation-settings.ts:292, is the only solicitation INSERT and writes location_id NULL), which is the same 'unreachable today' premise deviation 2 of this very branch proved false for `daily_send_cap`. Fix: one case seeding a location-scoped solicitation row with a different cap and asserting the account default still governs, plus a deterministic tie-break in the query.

findings.title: Stale count in the deviations file: deviation 1 says the tenant-scope entry count 'moves by +1'; at HEAD it moves by +2
findings.reason: Deviation 1 predates deviation 2's owner re-decision, which added the second allowlisted statement (`readResolvedAccountCaps`). HEAD moves ALLOWLIST_BASELINE 380 -> 382 with two added entries (`accounts`, `auto_approval_policies`), which the arch-review-log row states correctly. Deviation 1's merge-order conclusion is unaffected — only ours moves the baseline either way — so this is a reader trap rather than a defect: anyone verifying the baseline against deviation 1 computes 381.

findings.title: The intake edge case naming `pending_payment` has no case; only `cancelled` and `past_due` are exercised
